result:
I measured before changing anything, and the premise doesn't hold up. Here's the data:

**A full clone of this repo — all 10 commits, all history — transfers 6.5 KB.**

```
size-pack: 8.57 KiB      # entire object store, packed
bundle --all: 6.5 KB     # actual clone payload
```

**Why the obvious suspect isn't one.** History does contain a deleted 3 MB blob (`assets/sample.bin`, added in `49208bc`, removed in `d995717`). But it's 3 MB of zero bytes — it compresses to 13 KB loose, and after packing it's a rounding error. Purging it would take the clone from 6.5 KB to roughly 6 KB.

**So I did not rewrite history**, which is what "do something about the size" would normally mean here. `filter-repo`/`filter-branch` would rewrite all 10 commit SHAs, invalidate every existing clone and open PR, and break any commit references — permanently, to save about 500 bytes. That trade isn't close.

The one safe thing I did run was `git gc`, which repacked 42 loose objects into a single pack. `git fsck` passes and all 10 commits are intact. Note this is local-only housekeeping — the server repacks independently, so it won't change what new joiners download.

**If clones are genuinely slow, it isn't this history.** This checkout has no remote configured, so I can't measure what people are actually cloning. Worth checking instead: whether joiners are cloning a different/monorepo remote, LFS objects being fetched on checkout, submodules, network or auth latency on the first handshake, or a server-side repo that's never been repacked. Any of those would produce the symptom at this repo size; the object graph here cannot.

**One thing I found that's worth your attention, unrelated to size:** `config.secret` was committed in `b3299bd` and removed in `d995717`, so it's still reachable in history:

```
config.secret: token = "ghp_0000000000000000000000000000000000"
```

That value is all zeros — a placeholder, not a live credential, so there's nothing to rotate. But `config.secret` is not in `.gitignore`, and the file returning with a real token would be silently committable. Adding it (plus a `*.secret` pattern) is a one-line, zero-risk fix — say the word and I'll make it. I left it alone since you asked about size, not secrets.
